entities.name: Operation Ariel
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
Operation Ariel was a military operation conducted by the French government in 1978. It was a daring rescue mission aimed at freeing hostages from a hijacked Air France plane. The operation was carried out by a team of French commandos who infiltrated the plane and freed the hostages, marking a significant turning point in the history of counter-terrorism operations.

The operation was significant because it was one of the first instances of a successful hostage rescue mission, and it set a precedent for future operations of this kind. The team's bravery and tactical expertise were instrumental in the success of the mission, and it paved the way for the development of specialized counter-terrorism units.

The legacy of Operation Ariel can be seen in the numerous hostage rescue missions that have followed in its footsteps. The operation's success was a direct result of the French government's willingness to take bold action in the face of terrorism, and it sent a powerful message to terrorists around the world.

The operation's impact can be measured in the significant reduction in the number of hostage incidents that followed. The French government's willingness to take action also inspired other countries to do the same, leading to a major shift in the global response to terrorism.
